fightin_words.method: Fightin' Words (Monroe et al. 2008), informative-Dirichlet-prior log-odds

sources.reason: CONFIRMED this session directly from data/processed/controlled_eval.jsonl: all 150 live Quadrant A rows already have source=='HarmBench' verbatim. Because the Fightin' Words reference corpus is H = A union B, HarmBench house style is BY CONSTRUCTION part of the high-cue reference the C arm is supposed to sit in the low-similarity tail of -- this is a structural problem, not just a deduplication problem, and re-using HarmBench for C-source-authored risks both (a) direct A-equals-C identity collisions and (b) candidates that can never plausibly score into Q10/Q25/Q40 because they share A's own distribution. Prior session declared this arm blocked purely on CSV availability; that framing understates the issue. (Acquisition itself is low-risk given reachable domains; the exclusion above is a methodological/design judgment, not an access constraint.)

sources.reason: Hand-authored short directive-style goals, not naturally-occurring user text. Multiple independent downstream papers found this session note substantial templated repetition within the 520-item set (several papers prefer curated 50-200 item subsets for exactly this reason) -- an intra-source near-duplicate pass would be needed before drawing a low-similarity-tail sample, not just a check against training data. Also partially embedded inside JBB-Behaviors (see file_overlaps).

sources.reason: CONFIRMED from the source paper's own description this session: instructions were produced by GPT-4 generation followed by human filtering -- this is LLM-generated content, not unchanged human-authored external text, so it does not cleanly satisfy 'unchanged from an external source' in spirit (the released file is a fixed artifact, but the underlying authorship is model-generated). Independent citing literature also notes roughly 90% of items are easily/trivially refused by mainstream LLMs, i.e. many rows are mild or borderline rather than clearly harmful-assistance requests -- a real risk against condition 2 (harmful or clearly requesting harmful assistance) for a nontrivial fraction of rows. Usable only as a labeled-provenance supplementary pool with per-item severity review.

sources.reason: The clearest genuinely naturally-occurring (not benchmark-authored) source among everything reviewed this session: prompts scraped from real Reddit/Discord/prompt-sharing communities Dec 2022-Dec 2023 with human-verified jailbreak tagging. BUT the dominant record type is a jailbreak WRAPPER/persona template, not a complete harmful request on its own -- it typically fails condition 1 (complete and user-facing) and condition 3 (understandable without hidden context, since the wrapper alone doesn't specify the harmful ask) until paired with a payload question, which this project's own docstrings would call a transformation/wrapper, not source-authored. A minority of entries ARE standalone complete harmful requests and would need per-item manual identification rather than a bulk pull. Explicit content warning in the source repo; research-use only. (File access is low-risk; the per-item wrapper-vs-complete-prompt screening burden is a downstream curation cost, not an acquisition-risk factor.)

file_overlaps: Quadrant A (150/150 live rows) is exactly and entirely HarmBench-sourced (verified directly against data/processed/controlled_eval.jsonl this session) -- drawing C-source-authored candidates from HarmBench risks direct A/C identity collisions and, more fundamentally, house-style leakage into the H=A∪B reference corpus that the low-similarity-tail selection criterion is defined against.

JBB-Behaviors is ~18% AdvBench-derived and ~27% HarmBench-derived (per-row 'Source' field in the dataset itself); only the ~55% 'Original' rows are non-overlapping with the AdvBench and HarmBench families also under consideration.

This project's existing C1 pipeline (src/data_pipeline/quadrant_c_pipeline.py) already consumes 155 StrongREJECT forbidden_prompt rows as source_prompt (104 currently live as c_paired) -- any c_source_authored use of StrongREJECT needs a disjoint sample (different source_ids) to avoid the same item appearing under both construction types.

SORRY-Bench's own base 440-item set is itself aggregated from roughly 10 prior datasets per its paper, which plausibly include some of the same families already under consideration here (e.g. AdvBench-style or Do-Not-Answer-style items) -- unlike StrongREJECT, SORRY-Bench does not appear to expose a clean per-row provenance tag, so drawing from SORRY-Bench alongside AdvBench/Do-Not-Answer could silently reintroduce duplicate underlying content.

This project's own secondary C3 set (CASE-Bench) was built on an access basis its own summary.json records as 'user-attested SORRY-Bench access, not independently verifiable by this pipeline' -- i.e. if SORRY-Bench access exists at all in this project's operating history, it has already been implicitly exercised once for a different purpose, without independent verification.
